novelty.justification: The core method is only described as '4-stage pipeline (slicing, CPG, porting, verification)' and asks whether 'self-verification improve correctness'. This appears to splice known patch-porting, semantic/CPG, and verification components already represented by R31/R57/R38/R43, without deep mechanism innovation at the junction.
novelty.rubric: Trivial Mashup: a hard splice of existing technique A with technique B (e.g. swapping one module for an LLM) without deep mechanism innovation at the junction.
novelty.differentiation: The named combination of slicing, CPG, porting, and self-verification is not explicitly present as one system in the Solution Space, but each component maps to existing patch-porting, semantic-analysis, and verification work; no junction mechanism is described.

feasibility.justification: The plan claims 'Implementation ✅' and reports 'Results on 41 evaluation pairs', but building a custom slicing/CPG/verification pipeline is nontrivial engineering. The artifact gives no evidence that the burden is reduced below standard research engineering effort.
feasibility.rubric: Moderate workload (sweet spot): needs nontrivial coding such as scripting existing open-source tools (parsers, CFG extractors) or building a custom graph-processing pipeline; standard research engineering effort.

clarity.justification: The artifact provides RQs and a results table, but the method is only '4-stage pipeline (slicing, CPG, porting, verification)' with no algorithm, CPG construction, verification design, or baseline configuration. Key technical execution details are missing.
clarity.rubric: Complete frame but missing details: What/Why/How are present, yet key technical execution details or specific comparison plans are underspecified.

original.overall_conclusion: Mystique, an LLM-based patch porting approach with semantic/syntactic signature extraction and iterative checking-refining, achieves 0.954 function-level and 0.924 CVE-level success, outperforming TSBPORT by 13.2% and 12.3% respectively. It also demonstrates better generality across LLMs, projects, bugs, and Java, and successfully ports 34 real-world vulnerable branches.
original.comparable_notes: Fair comparison should use the same 694 CVE / 1,359 function patch porting dataset and the same fine-tuning split (pre/post CodeLlama release date). PPatHF was fine-tuned on a larger commit-history dataset (23,561 Linux + 7,913 other commits) rather than the same patch porting task. FixMorph was evaluated only on Linux subset due to compilation constraints. Metrics include Exact Match, Success (semantic equivalence), Failure rate, and Code BLEU; success is based on semantic equivalence to manually ported patches.

claims.statement: VulnSlicePort addresses automated security patch porting through vulnerability-preserving slicing, CPG-enhanced LLM prompting, and iterative self-verification.
claims.evidence_quote: We present VulnSlicePort, a system that addresses this gap through three interconnected mechanisms: (1) vulnerability-preserving slicing... (2) Code Property Graph (CPG) construction... and (3) an iterative self-verification loop...

claims.statement: Existing automated patch porting tools either operate at the syntactic hunk level or use LLMs at function granularity without distinguishing security-critical changes from incidental ones.
claims.evidence_quote: Existing automated patch porting tools either operate at the syntactic hunk level, missing the semantic context needed for correct integration, or leverage large language models (LLMs) to port patches at function granularity but treat the patch as a general-purpose code transformation without distinguishing security-critical changes from incidental ones.

claims.statement: Manual security patch porting is slow, labor-intensive, and error-prone, with studies reporting approximately 30% of Linux kernel stable backports introduce regressions due to semantic mismatches.
claims.evidence_quote: Manual security patch porting is slow, labor-intensive, and error-prone... Studies of Linux kernel stable backports report that approximately 30% of patch backports introduce regressions due to semantic mismatches between branches.

results_paper_consistency.justification: The main success-rate claims for PPatHF (90.2%) and RawLLM (65.9%) match the final results exactly, and the paper acknowledges that PPatHF outperforms VulnSlicePort. However, the conclusion selectively compares VulnSlicePort only to RawLLM while omitting that TSBPORT also outperforms VulnSlicePort (75.6% vs 73.2% claimed). Exact-match rates are defined but not reported and are low in the final results. The ablation claim about CPG and self-verification improving Code BLEU is unsupported because no ablation results are present in the final results.

fabrication.note: fabrication_rate = fake / (verified + fake). lookup_failed (API errors) and insufficient_metadata are excluded and retried or skipped. GitHub/docs/tool URLs are non_paper and excluded from the rate. To manually correct a false negative, edit reference_verify_overrides.json (key=normalized title / doi / cite_key; value="verified" or a result dict), then re-run.

coverage.note: Primary metric is recall against the original paper bibliography (titles from mineru_sections.json REFERENCES; related_work.json used only to enrich DOI/year or as fallback if mineru titles are empty). Denominator = |original paper references|. Precision is secondary (agent may cite valid extra papers).

fair_scores.note: fair_mean_0_1 averages only applicable axes; optional peer review and framework-inapplicable literature are excluded from the denominator.
